title: AC1024 GEODATA version-2 CIVIL tail specification conflict

provenance.author: Locally authored from scratch with ezdxf 1.4.5; same mesh author tool as p4-ac1027-geodata-mesh-selected-graph-2026-11-04.json. ODA File Converter 27.1.0 wrote the ACAD2010 DWG and DXF pair. No fixture added.

authority: ODA v5.4.1 section 20.4.78 describes the CIVIL block under the condition DWG version R21 or lower but also says AutoCAD 2010 always writes civil data. AutoCAD 2010 is AC1024/R24 and is excluded by the first statement but included by the second. The source shows the former profile; this evidence alone cannot choose authoritative semantics. The same section calls north direction 3RD while LibreDWG reports 2RD for this source; that discrepancy is not resolved here.

observedPhysicalFrame.graph: BLOCK_RECORD 0x17 owns extension dictionary 0x2F; dictionary entry ACAD_GEOGRAPHICDATA points to GEODATA 0x30; GEODATA owner and reactor point to 0x2F, and host soft pointer to 0x17. LibreDWG, ODA DXF and ezdxf agree on class version 2 and the three-point, one-face mesh.
observedPhysicalFrame.frame: LibreDWG verbose trace: GEODATA body 5392 bytes, 53 handle bits, handle boundary bit 43083; extended split-string payload length 41738 bits with 33-bit length/presence footer, giving start bit 1312 (byte 164 bit 0).
observedPhysicalFrame.meshBoundary: The peer reports the mesh count ending at byte 64 bit 0, followed by three source/destination point pairs, each four raw 64-bit coordinates; their 96-byte span therefore ends at byte 160 bit 0. The peer displays unsigned-wrapped individual point offsets, so that endpoint is a derivation, not a directly printed point offset. The face count BL ends at byte 161 bit 2; face indices end at byte 161 bit 4, byte 162 bit 6, and byte 164 bit 0. Thus the peer-observed scalar end meets the calculated split-string start at bit 1312, leaving no scalar span for the documented CIVIL tail. Trace offsets are peer observations, not a separate certified bit parser.

currentLibrary: Historical baseline: the production parser required a CIVIL tail for AC1024 and rejected this source. Follow-up 2026-11-05: the parser now accepts only the observed AC1024/version-2 no-tail variant when the bounded body ends exactly after the mesh; AC1024/version-2 with a tail remains accepted, and AC1024/version-1 retains its tail requirement. This is a source-profile accommodation; no writer or strict-output gate changed.
reproduce: <scratch>/probe <scratch>/dwg/mesh.dwg; verify the input SHA-256 before and after the probe.

implementation.rule: For AC1024 object version 2 only, an exact body end after mesh faces denotes the witnessed no-tail profile. A nonempty remainder follows the existing fixed-tail decoder; a truncated tail still fails. AC1021 and AC1024 object version 1 behavior is unchanged.

generatedControl.change: Added an independently literalized AC1024 object-version-2 frame with no Civil tail alongside the existing AC1024 v1/v2 present-tail vectors and later-version no-tail vectors.

physicalWitness.producer: ODA File Converter 27.1.0 converted a locally authored ezdxf 1.4.5 ACAD2010 input; source and output pair hashes are in the provenance fields above.
physicalWitness.result: The local reader reports GEODATA version 2 with 3 mesh points and 1 face, publishes 157/157 source frames, and reports zero entity/object parse failures. Strict DXF output remains atomically refused because the source has a separate unclaimed 739-byte HEADER suffix beginning at offset 843; no DXF was created. The input SHA-256 is unchanged.

readerFollowup20261105.qualificationEffect: The exact AC1024 v2 no-tail reader profile is now supported by a physical producer witness plus literal boundary control. The ODA-spec contradiction, AC1024 v1/version breadth, native application behavior, writer fidelity, whole-document output, and geospatial semantics remain open; no support claim is promoted.

next: Resolve the AC1024 v1/v2 CIVIL-tail cross-product with an authoritative erratum or additional producer spans. Keep writer output and strict output for this source unchanged until that evidence is available; native geospatial semantics and the independent HEADER suffix gate also remain open.
